# Chapter 4: Type Design Guidelines — 4.5–4.7

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest, and rules that analyzers check only in part, marked "(partly checked)". Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 4.5 Static Class Design

- **FDG4016** DO use static classes sparingly. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4016
- **FDG4017** DO NOT treat static classes as a miscellaneous bucket. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4017
- **FDG4018** DO NOT declare or override instance members in static classes. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4018
- **FDG4019** DO declare static classes as sealed, abstract, and add a private instance constructor if your programming language does not have built-in support for static classes. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4019

## 4.6 Interface Design

- **FDG4020** DO define an interface if you need some common API to be supported by a set of types that includes value types. (not in test projects)
- **FDG4021** CONSIDER defining an interface if you need to support its functionality on types that already inherit from some other type. (not in test projects)
- **FDG4022** AVOID using marker interfaces (interfaces with no members). (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4022
- **FDG4023** DO provide at least one type that is an implementation of an interface. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4023
- **FDG4024** DO provide at least one API that consumes each interface you define (a method taking the interface as a parameter or a property typed as the interface). (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4024
- **FDG4025** DO NOT add members to an interface that has previously shipped. (library only) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4025

## 4.7 Struct Design

- **FDG4027** DO NOT define mutable value types. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4027
- **FDG4028** DO declare immutable value types with the `readonly` modifier. (partly checked) (not in test projects) [C# 7.2+] (alt: Before C# 7.2 there is no readonly struct; declare every instance field readonly.) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4028
- **FDG4030** DO ensure that a state where all instance data is set to zero, false, or null (as appropriate) is valid. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4030
- **FDG4031** DO NOT define ref-like value types (`ref struct` types), other than for specialized low-level purposes where performance is critical. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4031
- **FDG4032** DO implement `IEquatable<T>` on value types. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4032
- **FDG4033** DO NOT explicitly extend `System.ValueType`. In fact, most languages prevent this. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-5-to-4-7.md#fdg4033
